rationale: Repaired the live-stall experiment's basis. The first receipt (32cd246ad3824df0b808f51ef1d36182) parsed correctly and its raw events showed the intended behaviour, but every comparison came back unknown because my admission pinned exact fixture indexes (snapshot 6, staged commit 257, 251 entries) and the observed run produced snapshot 7, staged 255 and 248 entries, and because the control's applied-index assertion used a constant. The harness now also reports, in the returned control, whether its FSM stopped at the snapshot index, the observed FSM mutation channel capacity and whether the fixture's replay demand exceeds that observed capacity, and the successor asserts only schedule-independent operands.

scope.description: Live three-node cluster (A, B, C; in-memory transports and stores; timeouts scaled to 50ms) in which node A runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, is snapshotted early, receives 250 further committed entries so its staged commit index is far above that snapshot, is shut down while B and C retain a quorum, and is restarted from its own stores twice: once with the feature and MaxAppendEntries 1, once with the feature off.
assumptions: All state comes from normal operations: bootstrap {A,B,C} from A, election with leadership moved to B if needed, committed applies, a user Snapshot on A, further committed applies and a graceful Shutdown of A.

The feature is enabled on all nodes during the first life, which is what leaves a persisted commit index in A's log store; the snapshot stays where the harness took it because SnapshotInterval is 10 minutes.

The exact snapshot and commit indexes depend on scheduling (observed 6 or 7 for the snapshot and 248 to 251 entries to replay), so the experiment asserts only the schedule-independent facts and reports the rest as operands.
Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; the control uses the same stores with the feature off so fixture size, store speed and cluster state are excluded as causes.
The stalled constructor is abandoned and a fresh transport is created for each restart attempt.
excluded: No crash, process kill or on-disk store is exercised.
The stalled instance is not resumed and no supervision or application timeout is modelled.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds three InmemTransports (A, B, C) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts A, B and C with MockFSM, waits for a leader and transfers leadership to B if another node won. It applies five commands, waits until A has applied at least four entries, takes a user snapshot on A, applies 250 further commands and waits until A's staged commit index is at least 150 above that snapshot, then emits 'fixture' with the snapshot index, staged commit index, A's log last index, the entries the replay would cover, whether that exceeds 128, the cluster ids and the leader. It shuts A down, confirms a leader survives, and emits 'cluster_status' with whether the cluster is alive without A and whether the stalled restart returned. Each restart attempt creates a fresh transport for A, reconnects peers and calls NewRaft in a goroutine with a bounded window: 'stalled_restart' with the feature and MaxAppendEntries 1, then 'control_restart' with the feature off, whose event reports newraft_returned, state, last_applied, applied_at_snapshot, the observed fsmMutateCapacity and replay_exceeds_channel, followed by a 'control_restart_summary'. Event order: fixture, stalled_restart, cluster_status, control_restart, control_restart_summary.
semantic_changes: The control restart event now also reports applied_at_snapshot (whether its last applied index equals the snapshot index), the observed cap(r.fsmMutateCh) and replay_exceeds_channel (whether the fixture's entries_to_replay exceeds that observed capacity).

Admissions assert only schedule-independent facts (mode, cluster ids, leader, and that the replay demand exceeds the channel), and the control's applied-index predicate is a derived boolean rather than a constant comparison.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft startup path: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh before the constructor starts the only consumer, runFSM.

comparisons.description: A follower restarted with the feature over more committed entries than the channel can hold should finish NewRaft within the observation window.
Control: the same stores restarted without the feature should construct normally.
Control operand: without the replay the FSM stays at the snapshot index, so the difference is the replay rather than the accumulated gap.
Mechanism operand: the fixture's replay demand exceeds the capacity observed on the same node in the control run, so the stall condition was met even though the control constructs.
The remaining two voters keep a quorum while the restarted node cannot start.

experiment.revision_reason: The first revision's admission pinned exact fixture indexes and its control assertion used a constant, so a run whose schedule shifted the snapshot and commit indexes by one produced no correlation and no evaluated comparison. The successor keeps the same scenario and adds schedule-independent operands instead.
